claude.sample_unit: prospective SMS recruitment rounds (model development used 11,616 Nanjing SMS records)

links.outcome: Recall at new sites after fine-tuning with 10% local data
links.effect: Fine-tuning with 10% local data raised Suzhou RF recall from 0.67 to 0.77 and Yangzhou MLP recall from 0.58 to 0.68.
links.quote: Subsequent fine-tuning with 10% local data further enhanced performance on top of direct generalization (Suzhou RF recall increased to 0.77, Yangzhou MLP to 0.68), rather than compensating for any shortcomings of generalization.

links.outcome: Cross-site recall of Nanjing-trained models in Suzhou and Yangzhou
links.effect: Transferred RF recall was 0.67 in Suzhou vs 0.77 locally, and 0.63 in Yangzhou vs 0.64 locally. MLP recall was 0.63 and 0.58.
links.quote: Specifically, the RF model achieved a recall of 0.67 in Suzhou (compared to 0.77 with local optimization) and 0.63 in Yangzhou (versus 0.64 locally), while the MLP model attained recall scores of 0.63 and 0.58, respectively.

unlisted_practices: Incremental retraining of the model with newly collected data after each deployment round before the next round
Ensemble of MLP and RF with prioritized intersection for selecting outreach targets
Adjusting prediction thresholds to minimize overlap with conventional recruitment lists

openai.sample_unit: prospective recruitment rounds across three cities
models_evaluated: Integrated MLP and RF recruitment model

links.outcome: Recruitment success compared with conventional donor selection
links.effect: High-willingness donor recruitment success was 408.28%, 25.19%, and 47.31% higher than conventional methods in Nanjing, Suzhou, and Yangzhou, respectively.
links.quote: On average, the recruitment success rate for high-willingness donors was 408.28%, 25.19%, and 47.31% higher than that of conventional methods in Nanjing (χ 2 = 35.471, p = 0.000), Suzhou (χ 2 = 9.384, p = 0.009), and Yangzhou (χ 2 = 96.701, p = 0.000), respectively, as shown in Table 1 .

links.outcome: Donor prediction recall following local fine-tuning
links.effect: Fine-tuning with 10% local data increased Suzhou RF recall to 0.77 and Yangzhou MLP recall to 0.68.
links.quote: Subsequent fine-tuning with 10% local data further enhanced performance on top of direct generalization (Suzhou RF recall increased to 0.77, Yangzhou MLP to 0.68), rather than compensating for any shortcomings of generalization.

links.outcome: Variation in donor prediction recall across cities
links.effect: Recall differed between Suzhou and Yangzhou: RF 0.67 versus 0.63 and MLP 0.63 versus 0.58. Locally optimized RF recall was 0.77 and 0.64, respectively.
links.quote: Specifically, the RF model achieved a recall of 0.67 in Suzhou (compared to 0.77 with local optimization) and 0.63 in Yangzhou (versus 0.64 locally), while the MLP model attained recall scores of 0.63 and 0.58, respectively.

unlisted_practices: Prioritize eligible blood donors for SMS recruitment using predicted donation willingness.
Adjust donation-willingness thresholds to balance donor recall against unsuccessful SMS outreach and recruitment-list redundancy.
Use resampling and cost-sensitive learning to address severe class imbalance in donor-response prediction.

links.effect: fine-tuning with 10% local data improved Suzhou RF recall to 0.77 and Yangzhou MLP to 0.68
links.quote: Subsequent fine-tuning with 10% local data further enhanced performance on top of direct generalization (Suzhou RF recall increased to 0.77, Yangzhou MLP to 0.68), rather than compensating for any shortcomings of generalization.

links.effect: models achieved recall rates of 0.63 and 0.67 in Suzhou, and 0.58 and 0.63 in Yangzhou
links.quote: The fine-tuned models demonstrated good generalizability, achieving recall rates of 0.63 and 0.67 in Suzhou, and 0.58 and 0.63 in Yangzhou, respectively.

links.outcome: recruitment success rate in prospective validation
links.effect: increased the recruitment success rate for high-willingness donors by an average of 151.57%
links.quote: It increased the recruitment success rate for high-willingness donors by an average of 151.57% (up to 408.28% in Nanjing) while recruitment efficiency increased by an average of 96.52% (up to 138.75% in Yangzhou).

unlisted_practices: incremental learning to periodically fine-tune models using new local data after each recruitment round

screen.practice: local fine-tuning of model on new-site data before deployment
screen.reason: The study prospective evaluates an ML-based recruitment framework deployed across three cities, testing implementation/adaptation practices including local model fine-tuning with 10% local data and dynamic threshold adjustments to generalize donor recruitment.

primary.practice: local fine-tuning and dynamic threshold adjustment
